title: Quota broker degraded-rejoin protocol and fair unblocking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When the global quota broker becomes unavailable or partitioned (region outage, upgrade, or heavy GC), tenants currently receiving soft credits can either be abruptly throttled or receive uneven restorations that violate short-term fairness and SLOs. This ticket defines an automated degraded-mode rejoin protocol for quota brokers plus a deterministic, fair unblocking algorithm for local proxies so we can preserve latency SLOs and reduce customer-facing errors during broker outages and recovery windows.
background: Redwood uses a quota-broker + local-proxy architecture for token-level admission control. Local proxies request soft credit grants from the broker and reconcile leases periodically. Previous incidents showed (1) immediate hard drops when broker leases time out, (2) stampeding rejoin attempts after broker recovery causing transient overload, and (3) fairness skews where noisy tenants grabbed bulk restored credits. We need a protocol that covers outage entry, degraded operation, broker rejoin, and safe ramp-up that is SLO-aware and tenant-fair.
acceptance_criteria: Local proxies hold on to emergency soft credits when broker is unreachable and do not hard-throttle for 90s by default
Broker rejoin uses a measured, tenant-weighted ramp that restores <= 10% of prior peak per 10s per region by default (configurable)
Fairness: restoration is proportional to a tenant's recent served share with a floor to protect bursty small tenants
No stampeding: proxies use randomized, jittered reconnection with backoff and centralized reconciliation windows
Automated telemetry shows <5x spike in token rejection rate during rejoin windows compared to baseline and no more than 1.5x latency tail increase
Runbook updated with emergency steps and playbook for forced broker rollbacks.
design_decisions: Maintain emergency soft credits locally (configurable pool per proxy) to keep short-lived bursts below SLA-impacting rejection thresholds

Introduce a two-phase rejoin: (A) broker announces candidate-restore epoch with per-tenant quotas; (B) proxies fetch epoch metadata and perform paced restore respecting local in-flight and SLO pressure signals
Use proportional-fair restoration where target_restore = min(remaining_demand, alpha * recent_served_share + floor). alpha is tunable; default 0.6
Implement deterministic tie-breaking using tenant IDs hashed with epoch salt to avoid first-come bias and ensure reproducibility across proxies
Backpressure signals: proxies consider 95th latency, queue depth, and GPU token backlog to reduce restore aggressiveness
Circuit breaker integration: broker sets an availability flag; on transition to unavailable, proxies switch to degraded algorithm and emit events.
implementation_tasks: Add local emergency soft-credit pool to proxy (config + metrics): 2d
Broker: add rejoin-epoch API that returns per-tenant candidate restore amounts and epoch salt: 3d
Proxy: implement epoch-aware paced restoration logic with proportional-fair algorithm and deterministic tie-breaker: 3d
Proxy: jittered reconnection/backoff and leader-election avoidance heuristics: 1.5d
End-to-end tests with simulated broker partitions and timed recoveries: 2d
Chaos test harness: introduce partition + clock skew scenarios in staging: 2d
Dashboard + alerts: token rejection delta, restore spike rate, per-tenant unfairness metric (Gini of served shares): 1d
tradeoffs_and_risks: Keeping larger local emergency pools reduces customer-visible errors but increases risk of overspending capacity during prolonged broker outage
A conservative restore avoids stampeding but lengthens time to full capacity for tenants—may impact high-throughput customers after recovery
Deterministic tie-breaking prevents randomness but could be gamed if tenant IDs correlate with request arrival patterns; we mitigate via epoch salt rotation
Complex backpressure signals add operational surface area and tuning parameters; default safe thresholds are required to avoid misconfiguration.
testing_plan: Unit tests for proportional-fair math and deterministic ordering
Integration tests: simulate broker TTL expiry and ensure local proxies use emergency pool without immediate hard rejections
Staging chaos: run experiments with (a) complete broker partition for 120s, (b) partial partition (50% brokers), (c) broker recovery with leader rotation
Load tests: replay production token distribution traces and verify Gini unfairness < 0.12 during rejoin
SLO experiments: verify 99th latency and token rejection impact stays within targets under 3 outage profiles
Manual validation: customer shadowing with low-risk tenants to confirm behavior in pre-prod before wider rollout.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: start with proxies in 1 region (us-west-2) for 48h under full telemetry
Enable broker rejoin API in read-only mode in canary and verify epoch announcements without forcing restores
After 48h, enable paced restores for 10% of regions (staggered) and monitor metrics for 24h
If stable, increase to 50% regions; finally global enable after one week with rollback scripts ready
Rollback: broker can set epoch to zero and proxies drain emergency pool over bounded window; runbook lists commands.
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics: emergency_pool_usage_per_proxy, restore_epoch_rate, per_tenant_restore_amount, token_rejection_rate, restore_spike_factor
Alerts: restore_spike_factor > 3 for 5m, token_rejection_rate increase > 200% for 2m, served_share_gini > 0.25
Dashboards: per-region restore timeline, top-20 tenants by restored fraction, SLO impact view (errors + latency)
runbook: On broker outage detection: confirm broker availability flag, verify proxies switched to degraded mode, check emergency_pool_usage and remaining minutes of buffer
If emergency pools < 30% and outage > expected window: consider manual preemptive capacity reallocation (reserved pool) or escalate to infra
During rejoin: monitor restore_spike_factor; if alert fires, instruct broker to pause epoch announcements and roll back stripe-by-stripe
Post-recovery: run reconciliation job to detect double-restores and tombstone inconsistencies and report compromised tenants for manual review

Future: expose tenant self-service hints for throughput-sensitive customers to request a preferential fast-restoration path under contract
Keep an eye on costs: emergency pools consumed during long outages will increase unit spend; add billing knobs if needed
